description: For an organisation that wants to show what it does about AI literacy under Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. Give the role groups and, optionally, your own yes/partly/no answers per checklist question and the questions you have evidence on file for. Returns a status per step (the four steps of the European Commission Q&A plus being able to show it): unknown, open, partly or measures_reported; the evidence expected per question; the gaps in the file; the actions with priority; and related obligations that are not Article 4 (Articles 26, 27, 50 and 5). No score and no percentage: Article 4 asks for measures, not for a level. Without answers it returns the full checklist. Same rule set as the section on aidoptio.com. Statuses are based only on your own answers: an aid, not legal advice and not proof of meeting the AI Act. Deterministic: no model is called and the answers are not stored.

acts_on_its_own.description: true when an AI system acts on its own, for example an agent that sends emails.

ai_uses.description: How AI is used. recruitment-or-hr and credit-or-eligibility make the high-risk questions 4.1 to 4.6 a point to check.

answers.description: Your own answer per checklist question id, e.g. {"1.1": "yes", "2.4": "partly"}. Call the tool without answers to get the ids and the questions.

evidence_on_file.description: Ids of the questions you have evidence on file for. Leave out to skip the file check (dossier_gaps is then null).

high_risk_confirmed.description: true when you have established that the recruitment, HR or credit use is high-risk (Annex III, point 4 or 5). Then questions 4.1 to 4.6 get priority.

is_provider.description: true = provider, false = deployer, left out = not established yet.

lang.description: Language of the returned text: en (English, default) or nl (Dutch).

roles.description: Role groups that work with AI: office, management, hr-sales, board.

name: ai_literacy_scan
title: AI literacy scan (EU AI Act, Article 4)
